title: Read-only git cwd matcher conflates backslash with slash on POSIX
outcome: src/claude.rs claude_local_dir_match_key rewrites backslash to slash on every OS. On Unix, backslash is a legal filename character, so a command can cd to a different directory whose path contains a backslash while comparing equal to the delegation cwd that contains a slash. That defeats the exact-cwd git guard and can run otherwise read-only git against a repository whose config contains execution sinks. Fold separators only on Windows; preserve backslashes on Unix; add a Unix regression test that distinguishes the two paths.
acceptance: On POSIX, read-only git cwd matching preserves literal backslashes and refuses a backslash-containing directory when only its slash spelling matches the delegated cwd, with a regression covering this boundary.
On Windows, existing slash/backslash and case-insensitive same-directory matching remains accepted, with cfg-specific controls.

Required focused validation and independent Codex/Claude source review carry exact input/result references, with no outstanding Medium+ finding; and the standard full gate passes on the landed input on a POSIX host (the DL560 test-ref run) as well as on Windows.
